items_missed: Never got the customer's name. Six-minute call, inbound lead, and it ended with no name, no email, and no phone follow-up path.
No 'how are you today?' and no agenda statement of any kind.
Never actually confirmed date availability. Said 'Wednesday the nineteenth, okay. Let's see. Just one second' and then moved to zip codes without ever telling the customer whether that date was open.

The virtual walkthrough was offered and verbally agreed to - the customer said 'Sure' - and then never scheduled. No day, no time, no link, no follow-up commitment. The call reverted to a rate quote and ended.

Almost no discovery. Never asked about garage, storage unit, number of boxes, additional stops, stairs or floors at the destination, parking or access at either end, long walks or narrow hallways, or specialty items.
No moving-stressor question.
No 'pricing is super simple' framing.
Disassembly / reassembly never mentioned as included.
No Worries was given as a bare '$2,000 coverage' number with no framing that it repairs, replaces, or reimburses accidental damage.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned.
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch - credit card fees got named in passing but not the transportation fee, fuel surcharge, or assembly fee framing.

Never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and no 'does that make sense?' sense-check - which mattered here, because the customer had to interrupt with 'Wait, wait, wait' and re-confirm the pricing structure three separate times.

No estimate delivered at all. Never gave a typical time range for a 2,100 sqft one-story packing-and-moving job, and never framed how long the packing portion would add. The customer left with an hourly rate and no idea what the move would cost.
Quoted the travel fee as $70, the customer read it back as $75, and it was never corrected.
Said 'if you're doing it on a Tuesday then it's just the same rate' when the move day under discussion was Wednesday.
No Save Your Ass prep speech at all - nothing on prep shortening the move, no consolidation examples, no carload tip, on a packing job where prep advice has the most leverage.

Zero close. No attempt to book the move or the walkthrough, no 'no deposit required,' no confirmation email, no bolded detail list, no reply-with-corrections, no 'any other questions before I let you go?', no hours or callback info. The customer ended it herself with 'let me talk to my husband.'
No Ecobox referral, on a call where the customer asked directly about wardrobe boxes and packing materials.
No 60 cents per pound baseline to give the $2,000 No Worries figure any contrast.
top_strength: She led with the right process instinct - recognizing a 2,100 sqft packing-and-moving job needs a virtual walkthrough and raising it before quoting anything - and when the customer pushed back on pricing she stayed patient through three rounds of re-explaining the 15-minute increment structure, doing the $190 / 4 = $47.50 math out loud rather than brushing it off.
coaching_note: This call had the right idea and no finish. The customer said 'Sure' to the virtual walkthrough and Joanna never booked it - she never even got a name or an email - so a live inbound packing lead on a 2,100 sqft home walked away with nothing but an hourly rate. Next call: the moment someone agrees to a walkthrough, put a day and time on it and capture name and email before anything else, then let the walkthrough carry the discovery and the estimate.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and accommodating language throughout - 'no worries', 'I'd be glad to help you out with that' - and genuinely patient through repeated pricing questions, but with no name, no rapport moment, and a customer who had to say 'Wait, wait, wait' to keep up, it stayed transactional.
